payload.text: We have three shops in Lisbon and roughly thirty thousand titles in stock across them. Staff look prices up on a laminated sheet at the moment and it is chaos. I want two things. First, one shared stock view, so that a bookseller in Alfama can tell a customer whether Chiado has a copy, kept up to date when a sale happens on the till software we already run. Second, a trade-in tool that tells a bookseller what to offer for a second-hand book that somebody brings to the counter. The offer has to be fair to us and fair to the customer. New books are sold at the publisher's fixed price under Portuguese law and we do not discount them, so the trade-in tool is about second-hand stock only. Booksellers work from the shop iPads. I want it live before the Christmas season.

On the trade-in side: whatever the tool says, the bookseller can always override it. They have been doing this for twenty years and I am not taking that away from them. That part is not negotiable. But I do want to know how often they override it, so record that.
